missionCases.objective: Seat the floor NOTE between the powered belts
Carry the NOTE while raising the mechanism
Feed and deliver the NOTE through the speaker opening
Feed and deliver the NOTE through the speaker opening

risks.risk: Six scores in 120 s on 19 of 20 starts is not supported by simulation. From the firing station every one of 34 perturbed carried NOTES passes through the opening, but 31 (91%) shadow both speaker beams within 7 s; six in a row at that rate is about 57%. Across all 1742 perturbed shots of the campaign 1398 were delivered and 1290 counted. The count rate did not move with launcher speed (6.56 to 7.68 m/s) or with the speaker's counter drive speed; the friction of the speaker surfaces was not varied. The 3 uncounted NOTES at the firing station bounce out. Watched for 20 s, each enters 0.54 to 0.63 m past the opening, returns through the opening within 3 s without shadowing either beam and comes to rest on the carpet in front of the speaker. None counts late and none stays in the speaker (4 NOTES watched in all, one of them at 123 degrees: 0 counted late, 0 stayed, 4 bounced out). The owner's criterion, wholly through the opening and eventually counted, is NOT met for those 3 NOTES. That is an open finding for the owner. Nothing recorded at release separates them: launch speed, elevation, lateral velocity, peak height and opening margin all lie inside the range of the counted NOTES. They are the carries R02-inner, R03-center-mid and R03-outer, which bounce out in 15 to 18 percent of their deliveries across the campaign while five other carries never do, so the cause travels with the incoming NOTE state. NOTE attitude and spin at the opening were not compared. A NOTE that bounces out touches none of the counter parts that every counted NOTE touches. The frozen full-mission campaign at the trial station failed three of its first seven starts. What happens to a NOTE inside the speaker rests on assumed field conveyor speeds and friction, so the deciding evidence is a real speaker.
risks.evidence: scoring-window-04/summary.json; scoring-window-04/results/released-20s.jsonl, angle-123-20s.jsonl; scoring-window-04/shots/; counted-reset-power-02/run-R02-96.json, run-R03-96.json, run-R06-96.json

benchTest.measure: Starts out of 20 on a full field speaker that score six floor NOTES within 120 s

risks.risk: In simulation 31 of 34 perturbed NOTES delivered from the firing station are counted within 7 s (median 4.1 s, latest 5.2 s after the shot starts). The other 3 are not late: they bounce back out through the opening within 3 s and are never counted. Six scores on 19 of 20 starts needs more than 99 in 100. The delay and the bounce-outs are properties of the modelled speaker interior and are unmeasured.

benchTest.measure: Delivered NOTES out of 20 counted by a real speaker within 7 s of the shot

risks.risk: The cycle trials fired from y = 5.871 m, where the NOTE cleared the side of the opening by 17.6 mm and a 2 degree heading error or a 50 mm lateral error lost every shot. The release moves the firing lane to y = 5.821 m (56.7 mm smallest margin). There every shot is delivered over heading errors of -3 to 4 deg, lateral positions of 5.796 to 5.871 m and stations of 1.39 to 1.45 m from the alliance wall, one input changed at a time. Errors combine: at 122 degrees, 20 mm toward the side wall with 3 degrees of heading error let 1 of 34 NOTES count, while 2 degrees with the same 20 mm delivered and counted all 12 nominal NOTES. The bench values are therefore the combined window, not the single-input one. The rear bumper is 35 mm from the subwoofer at the firing station, and stations nearer the wall were not fired. Chassis tracking to that window is unmeasured.

benchTest.measure: Largest heading error at the firing station over 20 autonomous arrivals

risks.risk: With 2 degrees of heading error present, delivery and counting held at 20 mm of lateral error either way on the nominal NOTES. From the trial lane, 50 mm toward the side wall lost every NOTE. Lateral tracking is unmeasured.

benchTest.measure: Largest lateral error at the firing station over 20 autonomous arrivals

risks.risk: At 122 degrees delivery holds 30 mm farther from the alliance wall with 32.2 mm of opening margin and 60 mm farther with 7.6 mm; at 100 mm farther 16 of 34 NOTES miss the opening.

benchTest.measure: Largest fore-aft error at the firing station over 20 autonomous arrivals

risks.risk: Delivery holds for cassette launch angles of 121 to 125 deg at the firing lane and fails at 120 and 126 deg. The edges are thin: 3.4 mm of opening margin at 121 degrees on 34 NOTES and 26.0 mm at 125 degrees on the six NOTES fired there. The release sets 122 degrees, the angle of the cycle trials: 1 degree above the thin low edge and 3 degrees below the high one. At 123 degrees the opening margin is larger (67.7 mm against 56.7 mm) but the nominal NOTES count 9 of 12 against 12 of 12, so 123 degrees is recorded as an alternative, not the setpoint. The campaign re-poses the launcher for other angles without re-running the lift. Detailed design puts the launch hard stop at the released angle.

benchTest.measure: Largest departure of the cassette launch angle from 122 degrees over 20 lifts to the stop

risks.risk: At the trial lane every perturbed NOTE is delivered for launcher commands of 6.56 to 7.68 m/s. On the nominal NOTES delivery holds down to 6.08 m/s, loses 1 of 6 at 5.92 m/s and loses every NOTE at 5.60 m/s and below. Belt speed at feed on a weak pack is unmeasured; the voltage test does not measure it.

benchTest.measure: Launch belt surface speed at feed on a weak pack, 6.88 m/s command

risks.risk: The whole-cycle check found both launch belt motor cans exactly at the NOTE's outer radius (177.8 mm from the cassette centre): the floor NOTE riding over the pickup lip passed them with 0.0004 mm. Revision A raises both motors 60 mm along the cassette normal on lengthened shafts; the checked cycle then clears them by more than 2.8 mm (15 mm sampled). The taller motor mount is not drawn and the pickup trial does not model the motors, so an off-centre NOTE meeting the lengthened shaft is untested. The 60 mm longer shaft is checked for clearance only: its whip and bearing support are not assessed.
risks.evidence: cad/preliminary-design/releases/1.0/step-revision.json; revise_step.py of the removed builder (Git history, commit 8e5d857)

benchTest.measure: Smallest gap between a NOTE picked up 50 mm off centre and either launch motor or its shaft

risks.risk: In start R02 the third NOTE left the speaker and entered the roboRIO envelope by up to 25.0 mm. No guard is drawn. Detailed design fits a guard over the electrical bay, charged to the unallocated reserve.

benchTest.measure: Deepest entry into the control-board envelope of a NOTE dropped from the speaker opening, guard fitted

risks.risk: During discharge the unloaded NOTE passes the right entry bearing bracket with 0.035 mm sampled clearance, bounded above 0.015 mm. NOTE tolerance or assembly error consumes it. Detailing relieves the bracket.

benchTest.measure: Smallest gap between a nominal NOTE and either entry bearing bracket through discharge

risks.risk: The free NOTE clears the slide motor package by a guaranteed 0.189 mm under a 12 m/s relative-speed bound.

benchTest.measure: Smallest gap between the NOTE and the slide motor package through pickup and lift

risks.risk: The centre intake belt indents the NOTE 7.56 to 7.67 mm against an assumed 8 mm one-sided limit. A 7 mm limit rejects both numerical resolutions. No force against indentation has been measured.

benchTest.measure: One-sided NOTE indentation under the centre intake belt at the seat

risks.risk: The unloaded NOTE overlaps each hard runner by up to 1.36 mm against a 2 mm planning limit. Runner height is adjustable; hard clearance and elastic compression are not yet separated.

benchTest.measure: One-sided NOTE indentation on either runner with the NOTE seated

risks.risk: The pickup seats the NOTE with the rigid blade tip 1.5 to 10 mm above the carpet and fails from 12 mm up (5 mm nominal). Carpet pile, tread compliance and chassis pitch under load are assumed.

benchTest.measure: Blade tip height above competition carpet with the cassette deployed and the robot loaded

risks.risk: The pickup seats a NOTE 50 mm off centre on either side and first fails at 100 mm on either side; no offset between was tried. Driver or vision alignment to that band is unmeasured.

benchTest.measure: Floor pickups out of 20 that seat within 2.82 s with the NOTE 50 mm off centre

risks.risk: The pickup seats the NOTE with a nose roller and pad grip coefficient of 0.30 or more and fails at 0.20 (0.45 assumed). The grip of the selected tread on a worn NOTE is unmeasured.

benchTest.measure: Measured grip coefficient of the nose tread on a competition NOTE

risks.risk: Departure waits for a seat beam held 40 ms. The sensor, its mount and its response to a deformed NOTE are not selected.

benchTest.measure: Seated NOTES out of 20 confirmed by the seat sensor within 0.2 s of seating

risks.risk: The NOTE stayed seated in every lift bracket, but the cover leaf leaves its cam stop by more than 1 degree when the lift is shorter than 1.8 s (0.13 degree at the released 4.8 s). The leaf spring and stop are assumed values.

benchTest.measure: Cover leaf overtravel past its cam stop during a 4.8 s loaded lift

risks.risk: With 39 A of other loads the governing loaded lift misses the pivot motor terminal demand by 0.089 V. The budget stages other loads to 25 A during the lift, which leaves 0.448 V. The revision A motor raise adds about 1 percent to the lifted moment and is not in that study: both figures were computed before the raise.

benchTest.measure: Battery current of all loads other than drive, pivot and slide during the loaded lift

risks.risk: The weak-pack bus falls to 8.344 V during feed and launch, 0.344 V above the 8 V floor. Pack model: 11.8 V open circuit and 27 milliohm.

benchTest.measure: Lowest bus voltage during a shot on a pack at 11.8 V open circuit

risks.risk: The upper inspection estimate is 56.344 kg against 56.699 kg: 0.355 kg of headroom, with a 3 to 6 kg unallocated reserve inside the estimate. The ledger starts from the study made before revision A and adds the lengthened launch shafts from the layout solids: 0.074 kg (9,425 mm3 of added shaft taken as steel at 7.85 g/cm3). The taller launch motor mounts are not drawn and not estimated. They, the control-board guard and detailing growth draw on that reserve.

benchTest.measure: Weighed inspection mass without battery and bumpers

risks.risk: Six scores followed by the climb on one 135 s clock leaves 0.18 s.
risks.closedBy: Mission rule from the strategic narrative: with 24 s left the robot leaves the scoring lane for the stage. The separate 24 s endgame case reaches power cut with 1.99 s remaining. A sixth score before the climb is not required.

risks.risk: After power cut the climb holds 11.5 mm above the carpet with the centre of gravity 40 mm ahead of nominal, 10.9 mm at 50 mm and 8.4 mm at 60 mm, against a 10 mm allowance. Rearward it passes to 120 mm. The centre of gravity is unmeasured.

benchTest.measure: Measured centre of gravity ahead of the nominal position, robot at gross mass

risks.risk: The climb latches and holds with a 6.5 s hoist ramp. A 5 s ramp leaves 6.9 mm of floor clearance and ramps of 4 s and shorter do not latch. The ramp is a controls setting with one passing value tried.

benchTest.measure: Lowest tire or bumper clearance during a 5 s disabled hold after a 6.5 s hoist ramp

risks.risk: Installed splice, drum dead end and bend strength of the 3 mm hoist lines are unqualified. The installed line target is 5.73 kN.

benchTest.measure: Proof load held by each terminated hoist line without slip or damage

risks.risk: Without take-up up to 227 mm of line pays out after the motor is disconnected. A 0.30 N m passive drum bias holds the modeled slack to 0.19 mm; the spring is a purchasing allowance.

benchTest.measure: Largest slack in either hoist line through full carriage travel, take-up fitted

risks.risk: Slide stop pins, the pitch lock and the keeper are ideal constraints in the climb trial. Pin capacity, catch engagement under load and wear are unproven. With the catch disabled the robot returns to the carpet.

benchTest.measure: Chassis drop during a 5 s disabled hold on the stops at 1.5 times robot weight

risks.risk: The removable slide link and index pin hold the cassette for hands-on battery service. Thread engagement, proof load and operator access are unverified.

benchTest.measure: Horizontal load held by the fitted slide link without movement

risks.risk: The straight 370 mm battery lift at the service index is not a checked case: the disconnected pack lead is not represented and the lift does not yet pass. The checked service case is the index pin withdrawal. An earlier service-lock study reported 5 mm smallest clearance for this lift; it has not been repeated on the revised layout.
risks.evidence: build.py --battery of the removed builder (Git history, commit 8e5d857)

benchTest.measure: Smallest gap around the battery through a straight lift at the service index, leads disconnected

risks.risk: The removable slide motor cartridge and the battery-service slide link are not among the layout solids, so their withdrawal paths are not in the checked cycle.

benchTest.measure: Smallest gap around the slide motor cartridge through its full withdrawal

risks.risk: No file of this release states the largest reach beyond the frame or the largest height through chain capture and hoist. At floor pickup the furthest forward point is 640.0 mm sampled (642.3 mm bounded) against the project front limit of 644.8 mm, which is 304.8 mm beyond the frame.

benchTest.measure: Largest reach beyond the frame perimeter through capture and hoist, measured on the first Fusion assembly

risks.risk: The layout STEP draws the cover leaf closed at the parked angle; the cam of the trials holds it open above 102 degrees.
risks.closedBy: The cam law governs: every cycle case moves the leaf by the cam and the recorded trace. The detailed model draws the leaf in its cam position at park.
